messages:
alex_k: FYI customer ACME Corp is seeing a sudden spike in 429s on their Dedicated capacity since ~08:10 UTC. They say latency also spiked. Example request id: req_0a9c3f. They reported autoscale didn't add nodes.

maria_ops: On it. Any errors in the gateway logs? Can you paste the exact response headers they got (x-tenant-quota / x-rate-limit)?

alex_k: Attaching their copy of headers: `x-tenant-id: acme-tenant`, `x-tenant-quota: 100`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-request-id: req_0a9c3f`. They claim they should be allowed ~5000 rps on Dedicated.

sre-liz: That x-tenant-quota of 100 looks wrong for dedicated pools — looks like someone applied a per-tenant global quota instead of per-pool. Could be a config push. Maria, can you check tenant config in the admin console?

maria_ops: Checking now... I see a quota record: tenant:acme-tenant -> quota:100 rps (scope: tenant-global). Screenshot incoming. This was created at 2026-01-21T07:12:10Z by infra-automation.

infra-bot: Deploy event recorded: config-release v2026.01.21-rc3 applied to quotas namespace by infra-automation at 2026-01-21T07:12:03Z.

alex_k: Customer says they've been on Dedicated since Dec and never had this limit. They started hitting errors only after 07:12 UTC. Can we temporarily raise quota while we investigate? They have an active contract.

sre-liz: Temporary mitigation: I've updated quota for tenant acme-tenant -> 10000 rps (scope: dedicated-pool) and removed the tenant-global 100 rps entry. Pushed to config-store and invalidated routing cache.

eng-oncall: Confirming change propagated: routing markers show acme-tenant -> pool:d0ded1 -> quota=10000. Also scaled up pool d0ded1 to 6 replicas due to backlog.

alex_k: Customer reports errors dropped to zero within ~30s of the change. They did see some token queueing but overall requests completed. Sending closure note. :thumbsup:

maria_ops: We should add a guard on the config release pipeline to prevent tenant-global quota overrides for dedicated tenants. Filed a quick ticket: CONF-3452.

sre-liz: Root cause summary for the incident channel: config-release accidentally applied a default tenant-global quota (100 rps) to some dedicated tenants. The config schema allowed ambiguous 'quota.scope' = unset, defaulted to tenant-global. Fixes: (1) add schema validation to reject unset scope for tenants with dedicated_pools, (2) roll back infra-automation patch to avoid reapplying, (3) add an alert when >0 tenants on Dedicated have quota < 1000 rps.

alex_k: Customer follow-up asks for repro steps so they can avoid app-level retries that worsen queueing. Maria, can you paste the repro playbook we used?

maria_ops: Repro steps we used internally: 1) In admin console, create quota record: tenant=acme-tenant, scope=tenant-global, limit=100 rps. 2) Send sustained request stream at 500 rps with auth header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to Dedicated endpoint for 2 minutes. 3) Observe 429s with `x-retry-after` and `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`. 4) Check routing cache: `GET /admin/v1/routing?tenant=acme-tenant` shows quota=100. 5) Apply fix: update record scope->dedicated-pool and set limit->10000, invalidate cache.

eng-oncall: Postmortem actions assigned: CONF-3452 (schema validation), OPS-998 (alerting), and a short runbook to onboard customers on expected quota types. I'll schedule a quick sync with infra automation.

alex_k: Thanks team. Marking thread resolved, will send customer the short technical summary and the mitigation timeline.
